Dated this the 9th day of January, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.)No.648/2014 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, North Paravur is the appellant herein.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, North Paravur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The 2 nd respondent in the O.P. is the respondent herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained on account of the accident that occurred on 29.6.2014.

According to the petitioner, on 29.6.2014, while she was riding pillion on a motorcycle bearing registration NoKL7-AQ-5796 along the Vypin-Munambam road, a car bearing registration No.KL 7BN 1300 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner dashed against her motorcycle and as a result of which, she fell down and sustained serious injuries.
The 2 nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
The evidence in the case consists of documentary evidence Exhibits A1 to A8, and X1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,77,100/-.
6. Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
8.

Heard Sri. A.V.M. Salahudin, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Smt. Sreekala,
the learned Standing Counsel for the 2 nd respondent.
9.
The Point: The petitioner was aged 32 years on the date of the accident, on 29.6.2014.
According to the petitioner, she was working as a teacher, earning a monthly salary of Rs.15,000/-.

However,
the Tribunal fixed her notional income at Rs.9,000/-.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the above notional income fixed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
She has produced a salary certificate along with the appeal, 2025:KER:5511 showing that her monthly salary was Rs.15,000/-.

sentences.text: It is true that the petitioner has produced a salary certificate along with the appeal.
However, no witness was examined to prove the said salary certificate.

Even as per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manger, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.
Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a Coolie during the year 2014 will come to Rs.9,500/- Considering the fact that the petitioner was working as a teacher in an unaided school

, I hold that the notional income of the petitioner can be fixed at Rs.12,000/-.
11.
In this case, the petitioner sustained superior and inferior pubic rami fracture of right side.
The petitioner has produced Exhibits A6 and A7 discharge summaries to show that she was admitted in the hospital on 29.6.2014 and discharged on 9.7.2014.
As per Exhibit X1 disability certificate, the medical board has assessed her disability at 2%.
Since, on the date of accident, she was aged 32 years, 40% of her income is to be added towards future prospects, and the multiplier to be applied is 16.
In the above circumstances, compensation towards loss of disability will come to Rs.64,512/-.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.27,000/- towards loss of earnings.
In this case, the petitioner sustained superior and inferior pubic rami fracture of right side.
The petitioner was admitted in the hospital on 29.6.2014 and discharged on 9.7.2014.
As per Exhibit X1 disability certificate, the medical board has assessed her disability at 2%.
Considering the facts, I hold that towards loss of earnings, the income for a period of six months can be awarded, which will come to Rs72,000/- (12,000x6).
13. Towards the head compensation for loss of amenities, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.6,000/-.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the period of treatment she had to undergo, the compensation awarded towards loss of amenities is on the lower side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.
14. Towards extra nourishment, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.6,000/-, which, is also on the lower side and hence it is enhanced to Rs15,000/-.
15. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
16. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total 2025:KER:5511 compensation of Rs.2,80,012/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 2nd respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs2,80,012/- (Rupees Two Lakh Eighty Thousand and Twelve Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till realisation, excluding interest for a period of 83 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
(Interest for the enhanced compensation is limited to 8%).
